key_insight: The paper introduces MRS-theory-based numerical methods that can efficiently find multiple statistical equilibria of two-dimensional turbulent flows, including symmetry-broken states on a sphere.
engineering_relevance: These methods improve practical prediction and interpretation of geophysical flow patterns by preserving all Casimir invariants and handling arbitrary initial vorticity distributions.
method: Canonical and microcanonical entropy-maximization solvers derived directly from Miller-Robert-Sommeria theory
Designed to detect multiple equilibria and search beyond zonal symmetry
Applied to a barotropically unstable zonal vorticity field on spherical geometry
evidence_signal: The authors report two equilibria from the test case: a zonal wavenumber-1 maximum-entropy state and a wavenumber-2 state that closely matches the time-integrated vorticity equation outcome.
watch_item: The approach may be computationally demanding for high-dimensional vorticity distributions and still requires careful handling of convergence when multiple equilibria coexist.
paper_title: New numerical methods for calculating statistical equilibria of two-dimensional turbulent flows, strictly based on the Miller-Robert-Sommeria theory
